source_name: MNB – Technikai kézikönyv (technical manual for PSPs, multifunctional-device initiated instant transfers)
why_relevant: Technical requirements manual for PSPs implementing qvik-type acceptance; explicitly tied to MNB Recommendation 3/2025 (IV.16) with a stated applicability date (approval interface chapter from 2025-06-01) — a concrete mandatory deadline artefact.

source_name: MNB – Tájékoztató a 575/2013/EU rendelet szerinti intézményi nyilvánosságrahozatali követelményekről
why_relevant: Supervisory guidance defining what banks must disclose and when; the schema against which each bank's Pillar 3 file can be checked, and a lead indicator of upcoming disclosure-template changes (EBA ITS 3.0).

source_name: MNB – BKR üzletszabályzat mellékletek mirrored on mnb.hu (approval trail)
why_relevant: MNB approves GIRO's BKR business rules and hosts annexes (e.g. annex 22 on payment-request-initiated instant transfer error and exception handling, effective 2024-09-01 / 2024-09-01 series). Confirms the approval + effective-date pipeline and provides a second retrieval path when giro.hu changes URLs.

source_name: MNB – Kriptoeszköz-szolgáltatók (CASP/MiCA) engedélyezés
why_relevant: MNB is the MiCA competent authority for Hungary; from 1 July 2025 CASPs need an MNB licence or an EU passport. A new, fast-moving licensed-actor population adjacent to payments, enumerable through the same Intézménykereső once entries appear.

source_name: Nemzeti Jogszabálytár (njt.hu) – consolidated MNB rendelet texts
why_relevant: Official consolidated legal text of MNB decrees with in-force dates and amendment history. MNB's own pages give the instrument; njt gives the authoritative hatályos version and amendment timeline needed for deadline tracking.

source_name: 1352/2022. (VII. 21.) Korm. határozat – government decision on the legislative/administrative coordination workflow
why_relevant: Sets the internal közigazgatási egyeztetés timetable — comments due within five working days of receipt, extendable, with the Prime Minister's Office administrative state secretary able to set up to thirty working days. Explains how compressed real-world comment windows on financial-sector drafts are, which drives how frequently the pipeline must poll.

source_name: MÁK – decentralised municipal account-keeping (decentralizált önkormányzati számlavezetés) programme page
why_relevant: A policy shift explicitly dated from 1 October 2025 that changes who keeps Hungarian municipal payment accounts. This is the demand driver behind a wave of municipal számlavezetés tenders and directly determines which banks/PSPs compete for public-sector payment flows.

source_name: Kovács Levente: 'A Magyar Bankszövetség első három évtizede' (association history paper)
why_relevant: Written by the association's own secretary-general; documents the membership structure over time, which affiliated interest bodies joined when (PVOE from 2017, cooperation agreements on shaping the legal environment), and how the self-regulatory apparatus was built. Best single background text for interpreting the association's institutional position.

source_name: GIROHáló service business rules (closed network access to clearing)
why_relevant: Defines the mandatory closed data-transmission network used by BKR/AFR/KHR participants; connectivity requirement changes cascade into bank infrastructure projects.

source_name: 2010. évi CXXXI. törvény (Jet.) – law on public participation in law-making
why_relevant: Defines the legal obligation, the forms of consultation (általános / közvetlen egyeztetés), what must be published, and the minimum comment window — the rulebook that tells a collector what SHOULD exist, so absence of a draft is itself a signal.

source_name: 301/2010. (XII. 23.) Korm. rendelet – publication and commenting of draft legislation and regulatory concepts
why_relevant: Implementing decree governing where and how drafts (jogszabálytervezetek, szabályozási koncepciók) must be published and commented on — defines the metadata a monitoring pipeline can rely on.

source_name: Hungarian acquirer merchant/POS acceptance manuals (proxy for card-scheme rules)
why_relevant: Card scheme rulebooks are member-confidential; acquirer-published 'Bankkártya elfogadói kézikönyv' documents restate scheme acceptance rules in Hungarian and are publicly downloadable — the best legal proxy for tracking scheme-mandated acceptance requirements at merchant/POS level.

source_name: Big-4 / tanácsadói magyar szabályozáskövető kiadványok (Deloitte HU, EY HU, Grant Thornton HU, KPMG HU)
why_relevant: A tanácsadók magyar nyelvű DORA/MiCA/AI Act összefoglalói strukturált határidő- és kötelezettségtáblákat adnak, és jelzik, hol tér el a magyar végrehajtás az EU-alaptól (pl. a magyar kriptoszabály szigorúbb, 2025.07.01. megfelelési határidővel). Kereskedelmi célú, ezért elfogult a sürgősség irányába.

source_name: A Kormány törvényalkotási programja (Government semi-annual legislative programme)
why_relevant: The forward-looking government plan listing which bills will be submitted in a given session (spring/autumn), with intended submission months. This is the earliest structured, official forward calendar available — months ahead of gazette publication — and it names financial-sector and EU-harmonisation items explicitly.

source_name: CIB Bank – Basel 3 nyilvánosságra hozatal (Pillar 3 report)
why_relevant: Adjacent regulated entity (outside the named seven but same peer group); its Pillar 3 report demonstrates the standard HU disclosure template and URL convention, useful as a comparator and as a pattern for locating peers' equivalents.

source_name: ABT Hungária — client news (OTP Bank qvik services)
why_relevant: Advisory/service firm publishing news items tied to OTP's qvik rollout — an example of the professional-services layer that names bank projects. Illustrates the wider class of Hungarian advisory firms whose news sections leak bank implementation detail.

source_name: Bank-side AFR/qvik customer notices (e.g. Oberbank Hungary AFR ügyféltájékoztató, MBH Duna Bank)
why_relevant: Smaller Hungarian banks publish detailed Hungarian-language AFR/qvik customer notices and T&C changes that reveal implementation timing, scope and sometimes the processing partner — an indirect read on the bank's technical dependencies where no procurement notice exists.

source_name: Compliance/RegTech vendor advisories on Hungary (Copla, CyberUpgrade, Legal Nodes)
why_relevant: Non-law-firm compliance advisories that translate Hungarian applications of DORA and MiCA into operational obligation lists — including the useful 'Mini DORA' (Art. 16 simplified ICT risk framework) distinction for Hungarian financial enterprises, and confirmation that MNB is the sole MiCA authority under Act VII of 2023. Lower authority than law firms but often clearer on scoping and dates; must always be verified against the primary instrument.

entity_name: Getting the Deal Through / Lexology GTDT
source_name: Getting the Deal Through / Lexology GTDT — Banking Regulation: Hungary (Debevoise-edited chapter, PDF)
why_relevant: Confirmed PDF of the Hungary banking-regulation chapter, including the MNB sanction range (HUF 100,000 to 2 billion) and supervisory powers. Useful baseline for calibrating how severe a reported fine is.

source_name: Google Cloud Customers — OTP Bank case study
why_relevant: Hyperscaler customer-reference page in which OTP Bank names MNB (Magyar Nemzeti Bank) requirements as a main driver for adopting Apigee API gateway — a textbook indirect trace of a compliance-driven buying decision at a private bank.

entity_name: Hungarian financial trade press enforcement coverage
source_name: Hungarian financial trade press enforcement coverage (Portfolio / Privátbankár / Pénzcentrum / Adózóna / Piac&Profit)
why_relevant: Aggregates and contextualises enforcement outcomes (GVH fine totals, MNB sanctions, PBT usage, Kúria rulings) and often surfaces cases before the primary register is updated. Treat as a discovery/triage layer, never as the record of fact.

entity_name: Hungarian law-firm client alerts on financial enforcement
source_name: Hungarian law-firm client alerts on financial enforcement (e.g. Maráczi, Fellegi & Társai)
why_relevant: Law-firm alerts interpret changes in sanctioning severity (e.g. sharply increased consumer-protection fine ceilings) and flag compliance deadlines earlier and more plainly than the regulators do. Treated as a class of source: several HU firms publish comparable banking/payments alerts.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség — Wikipédia entry (HU)
why_relevant: Cheap orientation layer: official name, founding, mandate wording, historical member changes (e.g. the National Savings Cooperatives Federation's 2008-2018 membership) and outbound links. Use only to generate leads and terminology, never as an authority.

source_name: MBH Befektetési Bank – kibocsátási program alaptájékoztató
why_relevant: Base prospectuses restate the regulatory environment, MREL/capital requirements and risk factors in prose — an unusually candid summary of which rules the issuer expects to bind it.

entity_name: Regulated institutions' own publication of MNB decisions served on them
source_name: Regulated institutions' own publication of MNB decisions served on them
why_relevant: MNB decisions frequently oblige the sanctioned institution to publish the decision on its own website, sometimes in English translation (observed: Decision No. H-PM-I-B-3/2025 hosted by BNP Paribas Hungary). This is a secondary retrieval path for decision full texts, and the only easy route to English versions. It also lets you detect decisions by monitoring bank websites even if the central register lags.

source_name: TenderHelp Hungary – tendering interfaces guide (HU/EN)
why_relevant: Bilingual practitioner guide explaining EKR mechanics, registration, and the relationship between EKR, Közbeszerzési Értesítő and TED. Useful for correctly designing the collection method and understanding what is and is not publicly visible without registration.

entity_name: Wise Budapest careers / syndicated financial-crime role ads
source_name: Wise Budapest careers / syndicated financial-crime role ads (builtin.com mirrors)
why_relevant: Wise runs a large Budapest financial-crime and regulatory-reporting operation; ads for SAR/financial-crime reporting specialists and a Regulatory Reporting Manager indicate where non-bank PSP compliance load is growing under MNB and multi-jurisdiction supervision. Syndicated mirrors are fetchable when the ATS is defended.
